title: Compositional Tuning of Dislocation Emission and Ductility in Ti-Nb-Based Alloys via Microstructure Control
hypothesis: By varying the Ti/Nb ratio in Ti-Nb-based alloys, the local stress state and dislocation emission behavior can be tuned to enhance ductility and mechanical performance, particularly in polycrystalline microstructures formed through laser powder bed fusion.
mechanism: At the microstructural scale, compositional variations will influence the distribution of stress and the energy barriers for dislocation emission, as observed in high-Ti/low-Mo alloys. This will affect the dislocation mobility and the onset of plastic deformation, leading to improved ductility and strength.
prediction: +15-25 % improvement in ductility and +10-20 % increase in dwell life under cyclic loading
computational_test: Phase-field modeling to compute the evolution of microstructure and stress distribution under varying Ti/Nb ratios; a result showing no change in microstructure or stress distribution despite compositional variation would falsify the hypothesis

title: Effect of Nb Content on Dislocation Dynamics and Strengthening in Mo-Nb-Ti Alloys

mechanism: At the atomic scale, higher Nb content increases the interstitial strengthening effect through stronger Ti-N bonds, which influences the Short-Range Ordering (SRO) in α-Ti. This modifies the basal slip systems and the interfacial strength between α and β phases, affecting dislocation motion and strengthening mechanisms.
prediction: +15-25 % dwell life under cyclic loading due to enhanced dislocation pinning and reduced slip system activity

mechanism: At the atomic scale, the interatomic potential of Zhou et al. [51] influences the energy landscape for dislocation loop formation. At the microstructural scale, the alloy class of MoNbTi and its comparison with other Ti-X alloys suggests that the presence of Mo and Nb modifies the phase stability and dislocation mobility, thereby affecting the nucleation barrier and strengthening mechanisms.
prediction: +10-20 % dwell life due to reduced dislocation loop nucleation barrier and enhanced strengthening, with a moderate temperature dependence

title: Effect of Substitutional Elements on Beta-phase Stability and Mechanical Behavior in Ti Alloys
hypothesis: The presence of substitutional elements such as Al, V, and Mo in Ti alloys influences the stability of the β phase by altering short-range ordering (SRO), which in turn affects the mechanical properties of the alloy. computational_test: DAMASK with Ti-6Al-4V-6 at.% Nb alloy parameters to simulate the stress relaxation behavior at 600°C and compare the predicted dwell life with the baseline Ti-6Al-4V.
